turns.question: Which companies disclosed exit or restructuring costs under 8-K Item 2.05, and what charges did each expect? Cite the filings.

report.markdown:
Based on SEC 8-K filings in the selected source (January 2025 – March 2026), six companies disclosed exit or restructuring costs under **Item 2.05**. The expected charges for each are summarized below.

| Company (Ticker) | Filing Date | Restructuring Action | Expected Charges | Key Details |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Applied Materials (AMAT)** | 2025-10-23 | Workforce reduction (~4% of global workforce) | **$160M – $180M** | Primarily severance and one-time termination benefits (cash) plus non-cash charges; most recognized in Q4 FY2025, plan completed in Q1 FY2026. [1] |
| **CrowdStrike (CRWD)** | 2025-05-07 | Strategic plan reducing ~500 roles (5% of workforce) | **$36M – $53M** | ~$7M in Q1 FY2026, remainder in Q2 FY2026; $19M–$26M cash (severance, benefits), $10M–$20M non-cash (stock-based comp). [1] |
| **Merck (MRK)** | 2025-07-29 | 2025 Restructuring Program (positions, real estate, manufacturing) | **~$3.0B cumulative pretax** | ~60% cash (employee separation, contract termination), ~40% non-cash (accelerated depreciation); actions largely done by end of 2027 (manufacturing by 2029); targets ~$1.7B annual savings by 2027. [2] |
| **Starbucks (SBUX)** | 2025-09-25 | Store closures & support organization transformation (“Back to Starbucks”) | **~$1.0B** | 90% North America; breakdown: ~$150M employee separation, ~$400M asset disposal/impairment, ~$450M accelerated ROU lease amortization; non-cash ~$400M, cash ~$600M; majority of closures by end of FY2025. [1] |
| **Pfizer (PFE)** | 2025-04-29 | Cost realignment program (“Realigning Our Cost Base”) | **~$1.6B through 2027** | One-time costs to achieve ~$1.2B additional savings by 2027; primarily cash for severance, digital enablement, implementation; total program targets ~$5.7B net savings through 2027. [1] |
| **Nike (NKE)** | 2026-03-05 | Organizational changes approved Feb 27, 2026 | **~$300M pre-tax (nine months ended Feb 28, 2026)** | Primarily employee severance; substantially all recognized in Q3 FY2026; estimates subject to local law requirements. [3] |

**Limitations** – The SEC filings source covers 8-Ks reporting Item 1.05 and the latest 8-Ks of the 100 most liquid stocks (Jan 2025 – Mar 2026). Other companies may have filed Item 2.05 disclosures outside this set. All figures are management estimates disclosed at the time of filing; actual charges may differ.

As part of this strategy, the Company assessed its existing store portfolio with respect to both whether coffeehouses had a viable path to offering the physical environment consistent with the brand and a clear path to financial performance. It will close those coffeehouses that do not meet these criteria. As the Company works to build a stronger and more resilient Starbucks and prioritizes investment closer to the coffeehouse and the customer, the Company is also further restructuring its support organization. The Company expects that a majority of the store closures will be completed by the end of this fiscal year. The Company estimates that it will incur approximately $1 billion related to the store closures, support organization transformation, and other restructuring activities, with 90% of the expenses attributable to the North America business. The Company further expects that a significant portion of these charges will be incurred in fiscal year 2025.
